title: Physiotherapist Job Performance and Organizational Citizenship Behaviors Analysis
author: Fu-I Hou
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bq2cmyaw

steps.title: Obtain Ethical Approval and Consent
steps.instruction: Secure approval from the Institutional Review Board (IRB) and obtain informed consent from all study subjects.

substeps.instruction: Obtain IRB approval from Kaohsiung Veterans General Hospital, Taiwan (IRB No.: VGHKS16-CT9-2).

steps.title: Distribute First Stage Questionnaires
steps.instruction: Distribute the first set of questionnaires to practicing physiotherapists in Taiwan, Penghu, and Kinmen to measure variables of the high-performance work system.

steps.title: Distribute Second Stage Questionnaires
steps.instruction: Administer the second questionnaire two months after the first stage to the same units to measure professional performance and other key variables.

substeps.instruction: Use the Impression Management Scale (from Kumar and Beyerlein).
Use the Organizational Citizenship Behavior Scale (from Polsakoff et al.).
Use the Job Performance Scale (from Motowidlo and Van Scotter).
Ensure responses are measured on a five-point Likert scale (1 = largely disagree to 5 = largely agree).

steps.title: Perform Initial Statistical Analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze the collected data using SPSS20 statistical software for Windows to verify reliability and correlations.

substeps.instruction: Calculate correlation coefficients between impression management, organizational citizenship behaviors, and job performance.

steps.title: Execute Hierarchical Linear Modeling (HLM)
steps.instruction: Construct a regression analysis using HLM 7.01 to explore individual and group-level effects.

substeps.instruction: Run a null model to calculate the intra-class correlation coefficient (ICC) to determine intergroup variance.
Perform intercepts-as-outcome and slope-as-outcome analysis to explore the impact of independent variables on dependent variables at the individual level.
Use overall level independent variables to explain the variability of dependent variables at the individual level.
